text:
erica_support: escalation from a customer (ACME) — since ~05:12 UTC their requests that specify us-west-2 are being routed to eu-west-1 and latency jumped to 700-1200ms. They see intermittent 502/504s. They ran a quick repro: `curl -v -H 'X-Client-Region: us-west-2' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate` and the traces show `x-served-region: eu-west-1` in the response headers.

erica_support: paste from customer logs: `req_id=abc123 account=acme ts=2026-03-17T05:12:08Z route=eu-west-1 latency=890ms status=200` they expected us-west-2 backend. Asked for immediate triage / potential rollback. @tom_sre @jay_platform

tom_sre: I see the same on our routing telemetry — bulk of that account's traffic started being rerouted at 05:11:54 UTC. Smart-routing service flagged the us-west-2 pool as unhealthy and elected eu-west-1 fallback.

tom_sre: digging into health checks: controller reports repeated probe failures for 3 hosts in us-west-2 between 05:09:40 and 05:11:58. The failures are short-lived (1-2m) but enough to trip our `consecutive_failures=2` policy.

tom_sre: relevant probe log excerpt:```
[05:09:41] probe->host=usw2-node-12 status=fail reason=probe_timeout duration_ms=280
[05:09:43] probe->host=usw2-node-07 status=fail reason=probe_timeout duration_ms=310
[05:10:02] probe->host=usw2-node-12 status=ok reason=200 duration_ms=45
[05:11:55] probe->host=usw2-node-03 status=fail reason=tls_alpn_negotiation duration_ms=360
```

tom_sre: note the timeout/ALPN negotiation timeouts — we recently changed the probe to use a full TLS handshake + ALPN check to validate the model-serving stack (PR #1424). That makes the probe sensitive to occasional TLS handshake tail latencies and can create false negatives.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout `edge-health-adjust` (PR 1424) finished at 2026-03-17T05:00:00Z in us-west-2.

jay_platform: yup that was the change — intended to reduce silent bad nodes but we may have over-tightened timeouts. Current probe_timeout_ms=250 and consecutive_failures=2.

jay_platform: immediate mitigation options: 1) flip probe back to TCP-only probe 2) increase probe timeout to 500ms and bump consecutive_failures to 4 3) add per-account routing pin for ACME to prefer local region for 1hr.

tom_sre: short-term I recommend (2) + (3). Increasing timeout avoids the false negatives while we validate ALPN stability, and pinning avoids customer-visible cross-region egress while we investigate. I'll prepare rollout.

erica_support: customer is asking about billing — they saw cross-region egress and want a credit if this is our fault. @billing_bot can you flag potential credit?

billing_bot: Created ticket BL-7789, flagged for support review. Please attach affected req_ids and timeframe.

erica_support: repro steps I used locally:```
curl -v -H 'X-Client-Region: us-west-2' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate -o /dev/null -w "%{redirect_url} %{http_code} %{time_total}\n" 
# then `http trace` on our edge: `cat /var/log/edge/routing.log | grep abc123`
```

erica_support: customer also provided an example request id: abc123 and a few more: def456, ghi789 between 05:11:50-05:12:30. Attached in ticket.

tom_sre: deploying hotfix to increase probe timeout to 500ms and set consecutive_failures=4 for us-west-2 probe group. Will route-policy prefer-local for account acme for 60 minutes. Rolling now.

tom_sre: rollout command: `./infractl rollout-config --scope=probe.us-west-2 --set probe_timeout_ms=500 --set consecutive_failures=4 --reason 'emergency revert of probe sensitivity'`

tom_sre: done — changes propagated to edge controllers at 05:18:02 UTC. Monitoring metrics...

tom_sre: telemetry shows health status recovered for the 3 nodes and smart-routing traffic to us-west-2 resumed by 05:19:10. Cross-region routes for account acme dropped to baseline.

erica_support: relayed update to customer, they confirm latency back to normal. They still want a billing review but appreciate the quick fix.

jay_platform: follow-ups: 1) revert PR 1424 and open a follow-up to implement ALPN check as an optional weighted signal (not hard fail) 2) add a safety guard to the probe service that prevents cascading failover for a pool with >N% of nodes flapping within M minutes 3) add a per-account emergency pin API for support.

tom_sre: opening ops task: OPS-592 (revert PR1424 + add optional ALPN mode + circuit-breaker on health flaps). I'll link dashboards and the probe logs.

erica_support: action items assigned. I'll draft customer credit proposal and attach BL-7789. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
